author: pawandhananjay
content: this is helpful. So seacast is more of an alternative for 8411 rather than waggle. Is that accurate?

author: cskiraly
content:
It is a bit more nuanced than that:
- on waggle: it is not an alternative, if we share the same understanding of Waggle
- 8411: Seacast is not an alternative to 8411. 8411 is a joint EIP to which different EIP authors have different ideas. Kamil has one, I have another one. There are technical differences between the two. Mine happens to derive from the line of work of FullDAS (sampled segmented erasure coded broadcast), cell-level messaging, Batch publishing, Informed Diffusion, Seacast, 8411. For his version he is the one to say, that's not on me 🙂

Anyway, this is not the right place to discuss the technicalities. We should do these in the networking repos and forums, otherwise it becomes just a communication mess.

author: .just_kk
content:
I am happy with whatever protocol version ACD agrees on. It could be mine, it could be seacast. 

But I cannot ignore the fact that seacast [spec](https://github.com/cskiraly/seacast-spec/blob/main/seacast.md) is huge while our goal is to introduce minimum required changes to p2p stack to be PQ ready ASAP.

I am convinced we should build on top of waggle. But I am not yet convinced we should build seacast.

That said If seacast is fine for everyone lets do it. But for now I just don't see enough evidence of why we should adapt it. I personally have simulations proving easier to understand [protocol](https://notes.ethereum.org/@kamilsa/rk_I4TMJme) is more efficient at least for proofs broadcast. But I dont want to start simulation methodology debate until we have a common agreement on how we even measure things
